Cc: none
Subject: Recurring E34 steam generator lockouts, scale on a soft water supply

Bought through ChefMarket (order CM-88213), delivered and commissioned 14 September at our bistro in Fitzroy. $14,800 inc GST. The listing says the steam generator was descaled and pressure tested, with a 6 month parts and labour warranty.

What's happened since:

- 14-22 Sept: E34 (steam generator low water level) logged 9 times. Service report SR-1190 on 22 Sept, level sensor replaced, inlet pressure recorded at 320 kPa and fine.
- Early Oct: E34 back 4 times in one week. Core probe also reading low. The oven said 63°C and our Thermapen said 70°C in a lamb shoulder, same result twice.
- 6 Oct: SR-1236. Steam generator found heavily scaled, descaled and flushed. Probe recalibrated to within 1 degree.
- Sat 24 Oct: E34 locked the oven out at 6.10pm with a full book of 60 covers. We finished the lamb on the stove and deck oven and took the pork belly off. That cost was ours.
- 27 Oct: E34 again, with further scale found.

Kelsall's position is that this is a site water issue and not covered by warranty, and they've invoiced $280 + GST ($308 inc) for the 27 Oct visit.

I rang the water authority about our supply. Fitzroy averages about 15 mg/L hardness as CaCO3, which they described as soft, among the softest in the country. Heavy scale 22 days after delivery on that water doesn't add up, especially on a unit sold as descaled and pressure tested. If the generator was properly descaled before it left the workshop, I'd like to know how it got to that state so quickly. Being told it's our water doesn't explain it.

To be fair, the service tech has been professional on every visit and the probe was sorted on 6 Oct. My issue is with the condition the unit arrived in and being charged a callout 6 weeks into a 6 month warranty. This is still open with the seller.

If you're considering a refurbished combi, get the descale and pressure test paperwork in writing before you buy. Also ask exactly what they'll treat as a warranty fault and what they'll call a site issue.

reasons: The piece says Kelsall has invoiced the callout, but Brett said it would be invoiced.
